source_text: Idcirco et in columba venit Spiritus sanctus: simplex animal et laetum, non felle amarum, non morsibus saevum, non unguium laceratione violentum, hospitia humana diligere, unius domus consortium nosse; cum generant, simul filios edere, cum commeant, volatibus invicem cohaerere, communi conversatione vitam suam degere, oris osculo concordiam pacis agnoscere, legem circa omnia unanimitatis implere. Haec est in Ecclesia noscenda simplicitas, haec charitas obtinenda, ut columbas dilectio fraternitatis imitetur, ut mansuetudo et lenitas agnis et ovibus aequetur. Quid facit in pectore christiano luporum feritas et canum rabies et venenum lethale serpentum et cruenta saevitia bestiarum? Gratulandum est cum tales de Ecclesia separantur, ne columbas, ne oves Christi saeva sua et venenata contagione praedentur. Cohaerere et conjungi non potest amaritudo cum dulcedine, caligo cum lumine, pluvia cum serenitate, pugna cum pace, cum foecunditate sterilitas, cum fontibus siccitas, cum tranquillitate tempestas. Nemo existimet bonos de Ecclesia posse discedere: triticum non rapit ventus, nec arborem solida radice fundatam procella subvertit; inanes paleae tempestate jactantur, invalidae arbores turbinis incursione evertuntur. Hos execratur et percutit Joannes apostolus dicens: Ex nobis exierunt, sed non fuerunt ex nobis: si enim fuissent ex nobis, mansissent utique nobiscum.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore also the Holy Spirit comes in a dove: a simple animal and a happy one, not bitter with gall, not savage with bites, not violent with claw laceration, to love human dwellings, to know the fellowship of one house; when they produce offspring, to bring up the young together, when they travel, to cohere in flights together, to spend their life in common conversation, to recognize the concord of peace with a kiss of the mouth, to fulfill the law of unanimity in all things. This simplicity is to be recognized in the Church, this charity is to be obtained, so that the love of doves may imitate fraternal love, so that gentleness and mildness may be equal to lambs and sheep. What does the savagery of wolves and the rage of dogs and the lethal poison of serpents and the bloody cruelty of beasts do in a Christian breast? It is to be congratulated when such people are separated from the Church, lest they devour the doves, lest they devour the sheep of Christ with their savage and poisonous contagion. Bitterness cannot cohere and be joined with sweetness, darkness with light, rain with serenity, fight with peace, sterility with fertility, dryness with springs, tempest with tranquility. Let no one think that good people can depart from the Church: the wind does not carry away wheat, nor does a storm overturn a tree founded on a solid root; empty chaff is tossed about by a tempest, weak trees are uprooted by the onset of a whirlwind. John the apostle execrates and strikes these people, saying: They went out from us, but they were not of us: for if they had been of us, they would certainly have remained with us.

pass_b_english: That is why the Holy Spirit also descended in the form of a dove — a simple, happy creature, neither bitter with gall nor savage with bites nor violent with claw-tearing. It loves human dwellings and knows the fellowship of a single household; when it breeds, the parents raise their young together; when it travels, the flock stays together in flight; it lives its whole life in common companionship, seals the concord of peace with a kiss of the mouth, and fulfills the law of unanimity in everything. This is the simplicity that must be recognized in the Church, and this is the charity that must be obtained, so that the love of doves may imitate brotherly love, and gentleness and mildness may equal the character of lambs and sheep. What place do the savagery of wolves, the rage of dogs, the lethal poison of serpents, and the bloody cruelty of beasts have in a Christian heart? It is a thing to rejoice when such people are separated from the Church, lest they devour the doves and the sheep of Christ with their savage and poisonous contagion. Bitterness cannot cohere and be joined with sweetness, darkness with light, rain with serenity, conflict with peace, sterility with fertility, dryness with springs, or tempest with tranquility. No one should think that good people can leave the Church: the wind does not carry away wheat, nor does a storm overturn a tree founded on a solid root; empty chaff is tossed about by a tempest, and weak trees are uprooted by the onslaught of a whirlwind. The apostle John condemns and strikes these people, saying, "They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would certainly have remained with us" (1 John 2:19).
